subject: series
synopsis: Akira Himekawa's manga adaptation of the beloved Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess game, faithfully translating the game's gothic, melancholic atmosphere and Link's journey through a world engulfed in twilight. Himekawa's detailed art and expanded characterization made this one of the more successful game-to-manga adaptations.
author: Akira Himekawa

subject: series
synopsis: A dark fantasy series exploring fear and moral complexity with atmospheric storytelling.

subject: series
synopsis: Jodorowsky and Janjetov's baroque sci-fi epic about an empire ruled by the creators of ultimate entertainment technology; shares DNA with The Incal and Metabarons, equally surreal and ambitious in scope.
author: Alejandro Jodorowsky

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman's landmark zombie apocalypse series following sheriff's deputy Rick Grimes as he leads a group of survivors through a world overrun by the undead, where the true monsters are other human beings. One of the best-selling independent comics of all time.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: Kousuke Oono's comedy manga follows Tatsu, a legendary yakuza known as 'the Immortal Dragon' who has retired to become a devoted stay-at-home husband. The humor entirely derives from his yakuza intensity applied to grocery shopping and housework.
author: Kousuke Oono

subject: series
synopsis: Caitlin Kittredge and Steven Sanders' Image Comics thriller about two strangers who discover they've both been activated as sleeper agents by a mysterious signal, forcing them to unravel who turned them into weapons and why, while trying to survive.
author: Caitlin Kittredge

subject: series
synopsis: Jean-Charles Kraehn's celebrated long-running series follows Doug Reese, a sailor and fixer working tramp steamers across the world's ports, drawn into crime, intrigue, and human drama at every stop. A masterwork of French bande dessinée adventure with rich characterization and impeccable nautical atmosphere.
author: Jean-Charles Kraehn

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Russell and Roberto Meli's Ablaze series: Roy Livingston, a down-on-his-luck former pet-store manager, becomes the first human sent on a one-way trip to Mars amid corporate spectacle.

subject: series
synopsis: Alan Moore and David Lloyd's masterwork of dystopian political fiction.
author: Alan Moore

subject: series
synopsis: Tomo Takeuchi's sports manga following Tatara Fujita, an aimless middle schooler who discovers ballroom dance and commits himself to it with fierce passion. Takeuchi's extraordinarily dynamic panel compositions capture movement and momentum in a way rarely attempted in manga, making the competitive dances as thrilling as any action sequence.
author: Tomo Takeuchi

subject: series
synopsis: Larry Hama and Andrea Di Vito's 2022 limited series revisiting Wolverine's 'Patch' alias from his Madripoor years — the eye-patched alter ego that let him operate in the criminal underworld. A nostalgic callback to the classic Wolverine limited series era.
author: Larry Hama

subject: series
synopsis: A space opera follow-up to the Rise and Fall of the Shi'ar Empire arc, pitting the Starjammers against the villainous Vulcan as he consolidates power over the Shi'ar Empire.
author: Christopher Yost

subject: series
synopsis: A manga adaptation of Futaro Yamada's historical ninja novel, likely illustrated with the elaborate ninja combat the Yagyu clan stories are known for. Set in feudal Japan with warring ninja clans.

subject: series
synopsis: Kazuki Funatsu's ecchi manga following a young man with the ability to see yokai spirits who is pursued by various supernatural females attracted to him. A lightweight paranormal romance built primarily around fanservice and supernatural creature designs.
author: Kazuki Funatsu

subject: series
synopsis: Naoshi Arakawa's emotionally devastating music manga follows piano prodigy Kousei Arima who can no longer hear his own playing after his mother's death, until he meets the vibrant violinist Kaori Miyazono. Famous for its gorgeous musical sequences and heartbreaking finale.
author: Naoshi Arakawa

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1994 event where Parallax attempts to restart the universe.
author: Dan Jurgens

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's anthology reprint series collecting American Marvel comics for British readers during the late 1960s, part of the early Marvel UK publishing venture that brought superhero comics to the UK market.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Bill Griffith's irreverent and philosophically dense newspaper strip featuring Zippy, a microcephalic wanderer who engages with American consumerism and cultural detritus with disarming clarity. One of the great alternative newspaper comics — deeply weird and sharply pointed.
author: Bill Griffith

subject: series
synopsis: Winsor McCay's early 20th-century newspaper strip depicting young Nemo's weekly dream adventures in fantastical architectural worlds of impossible beauty, rendered in astonishing Art Nouveau-influenced artwork. Among the most celebrated comics works ever created and a foundational text of the medium.
author: Winsor McCay

subject: series
synopsis: Aquaman volume 6 (2003-2006): Rick Veitch's mystical Lady of the Lake era, then Will Pfeifer's Sub Diego, ending as Sword of Atlantis.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1999 Deathlok, part of the short-lived M-Tech line: a new cyborg Deathlok, cancelled after 11 issues.

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's revival of the classic radio and pulp hero — The Shadow knows what evil lurks in the hearts of men — with multiple creative teams tackling the master of darkness in new 21st-century adventures.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 1967 ongoing starring Jim Corrigan as the wrathful Spirit of Vengeance, featuring some early classic Neal Adams art; the character has had multiple acclaimed revivals highlighting brutal divine justice.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Rob Liefeld's Image launch title. Historically significant as one of Image's founding books; the storytelling and characterization are largely incoherent, though Alan Moore's brief run salvaged it briefly.
author: Rob Liefeld

subject: series
synopsis: Chad Bowers and Jim Towe's 2017 Youngblood revival: a new generation of heroes in a world where superheroes are outlawed.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's digest adaptation of Ultimate Spider-Man vs. the Sinister Six, the animated series' fourth season.

subject: series
synopsis: Powers' second volume at Marvel's Icon (2009-2012): Walker and Pilgrim investigate superhuman crimes, including the murder of the hero Supershock.

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak's 2017 legacy-numbered Incredible Hulk: Amadeus Cho as the Hulk returns to Sakaar in Return to Planet Hulk.

subject: series
synopsis: Green Arrow's New 52 series (2011-2016): a rocky start, then Jeff Lemire and Andrea Sorrentino's acclaimed run reinventing Oliver Queen's mythos.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel UK's 1992 Knights of Pendragon: Union Jack, Albion and Captain Britain's allies battle the Bane in mythic British superheroics.
author: Dan Abnett, John Tomlinson

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2007 six-issue Sub-Mariner mini-series, Namor under suspicion after Civil War.

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Lemire and Pier Gallo's 2010 Superboy: Conner Kent in Smallville investigating strange local mysteries, a short, charming run.
author: Jeff Lemire

subject: series
synopsis: Scott Lobdell and Brett Booth's New 52 Teen Titans: Red Robin gathers Wonder Girl, Kid Flash and new heroes against N.O.W.H.E.R.E.

subject: series
synopsis: Antony Johnston and Christopher Mitten's post-apocalyptic Oni series: a century after the Big Wet, the wanderer Michael and fellow survivors seek the mythic A-Ree-Yass-I.
author: Antony Johnston

subject: series
synopsis: Titan's anthologies reprinting fiction, interviews and features from Star Wars Insider magazine.

subject: series
synopsis: Roman Dirge's gothic dark comedy about Lenore, a cute little dead girl whose innocent misadventures leave gruesome carnage behind.

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and Michael Avon Oeming's 2025 return to Powers, with Walker and Pilgrim back on the superhuman homicide beat.

subject: series
synopsis: Comico's 1985 adaptation of the Robotech Masters saga, the second generation of the Robotech TV series.

subject: series
synopsis: Yukinobu Hoshino's acclaimed hard science-fiction manga, an anthology charting humanity's expansion into the solar system and beyond across linked generational stories, in the tradition of Arthur C. Clarke.
author: Osamu Tezuka

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2099 anthology series featuring short stories about various characters in the dystopian corporate future of 2099. A showcase for minor 2099 figures between flagship title appearances, with variable creative quality.

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Onstad's landmark webcomic about anthropomorphic cats and other animals in a California suburb navigating existential crises, deep bromances, and absurdist adventures with extraordinary literary voice and emotional range. A defining achievement in webcomics that earned multiple Eisner nominations.
author: Chris Onstad

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's 1993 Aliens: Colonial Marines: insubordinate Lt. Joseph Henry and his squad face Xenomorphs on a remote colony.
author: Kelley Puckett, Chris Warner

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Jenkins and Leila Leiz's superhero series centers on a transgender woman discovering her powers while navigating family expectations and a dangerous new world of metahumans. One of Aftershock's most emotionally grounded books, balancing superhero spectacle with genuine personal stakes and a thoughtful portrayal of transition.
author: Paul Jenkins

subject: series
synopsis: Roberto Aguirre-Sacasa and Adam Pollina's 2008 Marvel Knights retelling of Warren Worthington's teenage origin as the X-Man Angel at a religious boarding school.

subject: series
synopsis: The continuing comic canonical adventures of Angel in the Buffyverse, following up on the television series Angel with stories approved by Joss Whedon.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marguerite Bennett and Eric Gapstur's Animosity spinoff exploring the broader world after all animals gained consciousness and speech — focusing on a society of evolved animals building a new civilization.
author: Marguerite Bennett

subject: series
synopsis: Nick Spencer and Ramón Rosanas's 2015 Ant-Man: ex-con Scott Lang moves to Miami to start a security business near his daughter Cassie, an underdog comedy.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series featuring Ant-Man and the Wasp in size-shifting adventures formatted for the Marvel Unlimited vertical reading experience.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: The third major cycle in Leo's acclaimed science fiction saga following human colonists on alien worlds, continuing storylines from Aldebaran and Betelgeuse. Features the same mix of survival drama, alien ecosystems, and character-driven exploration that made the earlier series essential European SF.
author: Leo

subject: series
synopsis: Emmanuel Guibert and Marc Boutavant's charming French children's comic series following Ariol, a donkey boy navigating school, friendships, and ordinary childhood adventures with wit and warmth. One of the finest children's graphic novel series published in Europe, translated beautifully into English by Papercutz.
author: Emmanuel Guibert

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Korean web manhwa: the Avengers come to Seoul, introducing the heroine White Fox.

subject: series
synopsis: Rick Remender's Marvel crossover event featuring a moral inversion affecting heroes and villains, exploring what happens when ethical alignments are reversed. An ambitious premise with some memorable character beats, weakened by its scale of tie-in requirements and uneven execution.
author: Rick Remender

subject: series
synopsis: Sam Hamm's sequel to his 2021 Batman '89 comic series, continuing adventures of Michael Keaton's cinematic Batman in the visual and tonal world of Tim Burton's films. A loving extension of the Burton era for fans who never wanted that version of Batman to end.
author: Sam Hamm

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid and Chris Samnee's 2024 Batman and Robin: Year One, revisiting Dick Grayson's first year as Robin beside a young Batman.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's late 1990s World's Finest limited series by Karl Kesel and Dave Taylor presenting key team-ups from the partnership's history, including early meetings and classic villain collaborations. An affectionate tribute to the World's Finest partnership tradition.
author: Karl Kesel

subject: series
synopsis: Christopher Priest's Rebirth Deathstroke (2016-2020): an intricate, sardonic family drama around Slade Wilson, his children and Defiance.

subject: series
synopsis: Boom!'s 2014 continuation of John Carpenter's film, co-written by Carpenter with Eric Powell, later Fred Van Lente: Jack Burton's supernatural misadventures in Chinatown.

subject: series
synopsis: A collected edition of the all-ages DC animated-style Shazam series, following Billy Batson and his sister Mary as they balance school and superheroics.
author: Art Baltazar

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns' landmark 2009 DC crossover event collected in trade format — the Black Lanterns' assault on the living DC Universe. Essential for DC event readers.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1994 collected editions of Blade the Vampire Hunter material, collecting stories of Eric Brooks the Dhampir vampire hunter. Published around the character's growing profile ahead of the 1998 Wesley Snipes film.
author: Ian Edginton

subject: series
synopsis: Majuro Kaname's dark romantic manga following two teenagers who are destined enemies — one chosen by Death, one chosen by Life — yet drawn irresistibly toward each other despite supernatural compulsion to destroy one another. A genre-blend of horror and romance with genuine tension.
author: Majuro Kaname

subject: series
synopsis: Kouichi Shimaboshi's manga reimagining of Leiji Matsumoto's iconic Captain Harlock for a new generation, updating the space pirate's design and adventures while preserving Matsumoto's themes of freedom, romanticism, and rebellion against oppressive order. A respectful new entry point for one of anime and manga's most legendary characters.
author: Leiji Matsumoto (original)

subject: series
synopsis: Stan Lee and Sharad Devarajan's Indian superhero created for Graphic India follows Raju Rai, a young scientist who discovers a powerful suit of armor that activates his chakra points. An interesting cultural experiment that brings Western superhero conventions to a distinctly South Asian mythological framework.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: Greg Pak and Fred Van Lente's story of Hercules returning with godlike power to battle the Chaos King, who seeks to destroy all of existence.
author: Greg Pak

subject: series
synopsis: Steve Foxe's 2024 mini follows Ben Reilly's Chasm persona in an underworld-adjacent Spider-Man spinoff, a competent villain-spotlight story building on established Chasm lore.
author: Steve Foxe

subject: series
synopsis: David Hine story following Colossus as he returns to Russia to investigate a deadly force connected to his bloodline.
author: David Hine

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Claremont's sequel tournament story forcing Earth's heroes to battle each other under alien observation.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2015 event series set on a planet that collects cities from destroyed timelines, forcing heroes from different DC Universes to fight each other. An ambitious concept that served as a vehicle for DC's move from New York to California while allowing creative teams to revisit beloved pre-Crisis continuities.

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's collected archives of Crime Does Not Pay (1942–1955) — one of the most successful and influential pre-code crime comics ever published, featuring lurid dramatizations of real criminals' lives with a winking moral. Edited by Charles Biro and Bob Wood, it defined American crime comics and directly inspired the Congressional hearings that led to the Comics Code.
author: Charles Biro, Bob Wood

subject: series
synopsis: Kris Wilson, Rob DenBleyker, Matt Melvin, and Dave McElfatrick's anarchic dark humor webcomic collection — raw, often shocking humor delivered in a deliberately crude art style. One of the most popular and controversial webcomics of the 2000s, celebrated for its willingness to find comedy in genuinely uncomfortable places.
author: Kris Wilson, Rob DenBleyker

subject: series
synopsis: A five-issue limited series focusing on Raven of the Teen Titans as she navigates college life while dealing with the return of her demonic father Trigon's influence. A character study mixing horror and superhero elements.
author: Marv Wolfman

subject: series
synopsis: Haruko Kumota's layered drama set in the world of rakugo — traditional Japanese comedic storytelling — follows an ex-convict who becomes apprenticed to the last great master and eventually inherits his legacy. A uniquely cultured manga about art, mortality, and the passing of traditions.
author: Haruko Kumota

subject: series
synopsis: Kiminori Wakasugi's absurdist music comedy follows mild-mannered Souichi Negishi, who secretly becomes Krauser II, the demonic frontman of extreme metal band Detroit Metal City. An expertly crafted one-joke comedy that somehow sustains its premise brilliantly across the whole run.
author: Kiminori Wakasugi

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's Disney anthology title collected classic and new stories featuring Mickey Mouse, Donald Duck, and other Disney characters, maintaining the high production standards of the Disney comics tradition. A quality preservation effort that makes classic European Disney material accessible to American readers.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Collected library edition of Disney Frozen comics in an oversized hardcover format.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Epic Collection reprinting volumes of Doctor Strange stories from the Bronze Age, collecting essential Lee/Ditko-era material through Steve Englehart and Frank Brunner's psychedelic 1970s run.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Minetaro Mochizuki's post-disaster survival manga follows survivors of a catastrophic tunnel collapse navigating a Japan plunged into darkness and ash. A relentlessly oppressive and psychologically intense survival horror work.
author: Minetaro Mochizuki

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman and Nick Dragotta's ambitious alternate-history epic in which Death — one of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse — rebels against his brethren and hunts for his lost son, reshaping a fractured United States defined by seven rival nations.
author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: Art Baltazar and Franco's Catalyst Prime series: a young alien crash-lands on Earth and becomes a superhero.

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Haberlin's hard science fiction series following the crew of humanity's first faster-than-light spacecraft as they explore distant star systems and make first contact with alien civilizations.
author: Brian Haberlin

subject: series
synopsis: Eric Trautmann's Dynamite revival of Flash Gordon in a fresh period-appropriate adventure capturing the 1930s pulp aesthetic of Alex Raymond's original strips.
author: Eric Trautmann

subject: series
synopsis: Hiroya Oku's (Gantz, Inuyashiki) manga follows a boy who falls for an adult film star, who then begins growing to kaiju size during mysterious global attacks. Features Oku's trademark shock value and photorealistic art.
author: Hiroya Oku

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Claremont's vision of the next generation of X-Men featuring the adult children of the classic team, offering a soft continuation of his long X-Men career in a fan-service-friendly but narratively modest package.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: The sequel to GeNEXT continuing the adventures of the second-generation X-Men, with Claremont deepening the cast's relationships and expanding their world.
author: Chris Claremont

subject: series
synopsis: A prehistoric spinoff of the popular Geronimo Stilton children's chapter book and comics franchise, following mouse ancestors in the Stone Age. Bright, energetic kids' comics in the Stilton house style.
author: Geronimo Stilton

subject: series
synopsis: Papercutz's all-ages adventure comics continue the beloved children's book mouse-journalist in original stories combining humor, mystery, and globe-trotting adventure. Faithful to Stilton's character and accessible to young readers, with enough wit to entertain parents reading alongside.
author: Geronimo Stilton

subject: series
synopsis: Supplemental comics to Phil and Kaja Foglio's steampunk webcomic Girl Genius, collecting bonus stories, behind-the-scenes material, and short adventures expanding the world of Agatha Heterodyne. For fans of the main series, essential.
author: Phil Foglio

subject: series
synopsis: Kurtis J. Wiebe and Riley Rossmo's dark fantasy noir set in a mysterious purgatorial town called Green Wake to which people are drawn after trauma, following two investigators trying to solve a murder in a place where nothing is as it seems.
author: Kurtis J. Wiebe

subject: series
synopsis: Zenescope's line-wide crossover event drew together its various Grimm Fairy Tales titles in a battle against the forces of darkness threatening all realms. Standard shared-universe event storytelling aimed squarely at fans of the publisher's mature-rated fantasy line, with characteristic Zenescope production values.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A GFT Oz universe anthology presenting standalone dark fantasy stories set in Zenescope's reimagined Oz, serving as supplementary material to the main Oz spinoff.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinite Comics digital series featuring the Guardians of the Galaxy, tied to the Awesome Mix persona from the films, in digital-exclusive adventures.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Kenichi Sonoda's second Gunsmith Cats series continuing Rally Vincent and Minnie May's bounty hunting adventures in Chicago, with Sonoda's detailed gun and car art even more technically refined in this follow-up.
author: Kenichi Sonoda

subject: series
synopsis: Gerard Jones' 1992 DC miniseries following Guy Gardner's acquisition of the Yellow Sinestro Ring and his emergence as a more independent, less overtly comedic superhero. An important transitional story that moved Gardner from comedic foil toward genuine character complexity.
author: Gerard Jones

subject: series
synopsis: Shuzo Oshimi's vampire manga follows a bullied boy who is bitten by a mysterious girl and begins transforming, caught between his human life and his growing vampiric urges. Quieter and more psychologically focused than typical vampire action fare.
author: Shuzo Oshimi

subject: series
synopsis: Andrew Vachss and various artists' Dark Horse crime anthology adapting stories from Vachss' prose fiction — hard-boiled crime tales featuring the child-protection work that characterized his Burke detective novels. Grittier and more committed to depicting exploitation and its consequences than typical crime comics.
author: Andrew Vachss

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 1974 black-and-white horror magazine, home to Gabriel the Devil Hunter and Satana alongside short horror stories.

subject: series
synopsis: Nanaki Nanao's fantasy action-comedy follows a seemingly overpowered human hero who enters a demon king competition claiming to hate humans, partnered with a suspicious demon noble. Praised for hiding genuine emotional depth and a surprisingly serious overarching plot beneath its comedic exterior.
author: Nanaki Nanao

subject: series
synopsis: Kouta Hirano's ultra-violent gothic action series follows Alucard, the most powerful vampire serving the British Hellsing Organization, as they battle the undead and a neo-Nazi vampire army. Famous for its extreme over-the-top action, darkly comedic tone, and memorable villain Millennium.
author: Kouta Hirano

subject: series
synopsis: A Markosia series about a mysterious character with supernatural elements and psychological depth.

subject: series
synopsis: Hideo Yamamoto's psychologically disturbing manga about a homeless man who undergoes experimental trepanation and begins seeing people as grotesque shapes that represent their psychological traumas. A deeply unsettling exploration of identity and perception.

subject: series
synopsis: Chica Umino's warm and melancholy josei comedy-drama follows a group of art college students navigating love triangles, career anxieties, and the bittersweet passage into adulthood. Beloved for its authentic emotional texture and beautifully observed characters.
author: Umino Chica

subject: series
synopsis: Graphic novel adaptations of Lauren Tarshis's bestselling I Survived chapter book series, dramatizing real historical disasters from a child protagonist's perspective. Engaging, age-appropriate historical drama for young readers.
author: Lauren Tarshis

subject: series
synopsis: Hideo Yamamoto's extremely violent manga following both a sadistic yakuza enforcer named Kakihara and a traumatized young man called Ichi who becomes an unwilling killing machine. A transgressive exercise in depicting human capacity for violence and self-destruction; important in the extreme manga canon but genuinely disturbing.
author: Hideo Yamamoto

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid and Kwanza Osajyefo's 2019 Humanoids H1 series: after a school shooting, students at a Phoenix high school gain powers and confront violence and policing.

subject: series
synopsis: Warren Ellis's dieselpunk science fiction miniseries set in an alternate 1956 where humanity abandoned space exploration and rocket pilots are washed-up relics living in a degraded spaceport ghetto, examining nostalgia, failure, and the death of the future through sharp, witty writing.
author: Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman's major crossover event pitting the Avengers against the cosmic Builders while Thanos secretly invades Earth seeking something hidden among the Illuminati's secrets.
author: Jonathan Hickman

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's all-ages Infinity Comics digital series featuring the animals of the Marvel universe — Thanos's cat, various pets — in comedic short-format adventures.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Hiroya Oku's (Gantz) superhero manga follows two people transformed by an alien crash — a terminally ill old man who becomes a selfless hero and a high school boy who becomes a remorseless killer. A sharp examination of what makes us human and how we choose to use power.
author: Hiroya Oku

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2010 JSA spinoff series focusing on a smaller, more action-oriented team of Justice Society members, running concurrently with the main JSA title. A solid but secondary JSA series that struggled to find a distinct identity from the main book.
author: Matthew Sturges

subject: series
synopsis: Dennis Hopeless's 2017 series following the time-displaced teenage Jean Grey preparing for the arrival of the Phoenix Force by training with other Phoenix hosts and wrestling with a destiny she wants to avoid.
author: Dennis Hopeless

subject: series
synopsis: Collected volumes of Cassandra Anderson's PSI Division cases — Alan Grant's stories of Mega-City One's most celebrated telepath judge, navigating psychic crime with flair, cynicism, and surprising humanity.
author: Alan Grant

subject: series
synopsis: Jeff Lemire's 2014 Canadian-themed Justice League series featuring a rotating roster including Animal Man, Green Arrow, Stargirl, and Martian Manhunter. Lemire's warm character work and interest in Canadian geography and mythology gave the book a distinctive identity.
author: Jeff Lemire

subject: series
synopsis: Homura Kawamoto's spinoff of Kakegurui follows Mary Saotome before she met Yumeko, as she navigates the gambling hierarchy of Hyakkaou Academy. Shares the main series' stylish psychological tension with a more grounded protagonist.
author: Homura Kawamoto

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series featuring Kang the Conqueror in a time-travel adventure formatted for the Marvel Unlimited vertical reading experience.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A spin-off anthology from Jolly R. Blackburn's beloved Knights of the Dinner Table universe, collecting additional stories and misadventures from Muncie's gaming community beyond the main series.
author: Jolly R. Blackburn

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's adaptation of Robert E. Howard's pre-Conan creation Kull, the Atlantean warrior who conquers the kingdom of Valusia and struggles to hold power against sorcerers, usurpers, and existential threats. The original Marvel series from the early 1970s drew on Howard's stories and original Kull material, part of Marvel's rich sword-and-sorcery lineup alongside Conan and Red Sonja.
author: Roy Thomas

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Benitez's steampunk series about a female cyborg detective in a Victorian-era world of airships and automatons. Benitez's lush, detailed art is the primary draw; the adventure stories are solid if not groundbreaking.
author: Joe Benitez

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series exploring Wolverine's long life in episodic format tied to the Krakoa Era, optimized for Marvel Unlimited's vertical reading.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series featuring Loki in contemporary earthly adventures formatted for the Marvel Unlimited platform.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Philippe Druillet's psychedelic space opera following the immortal wanderer Lone Sloane through baroque cosmic dimensions — one of the foundational works of European Heavy Metal-style science fantasy art.
author: Philippe Druillet

subject: series
synopsis: Fabrice Erre and Sylvain Savoia's educational Papercutz series following two children who time-travel through history with their teacher/guide, learning about historical periods through adventure. A charming approach to history education.
author: Fabrice Erre

subject: series
synopsis: Ashley Allen and Germán Peralta's 2025 Magik ongoing: Illyana Rasputin, sorceress of Limbo, faces new demonic threats after Krakoa.

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Massey and Robbi Rodriguez's Oni Press comedy series about two janitors who work at a supervillain research facility and have to deal with the absurd accidents and escaped experiments of their workplace. A clever workplace comedy set in a genre context.
author: Jim Massey

subject: series
synopsis: Rumiko Takahashi's romantic comedy-drama is one of the definitive manga romances, following Yusaku Godai, a struggling student who falls for Kyoko, the young widowed manager of his boarding house. Praised for its emotional authenticity, slow-burn tension, and surprisingly mature handling of grief and class.
author: Rumiko Takahashi

subject: series
synopsis: Nancy Butler's five-issue comics adaptation of Jane Austen's classic novel, faithfully rendering the wit and romantic drama of the original.
author: Nancy Butler

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's all-ages animated tie-in digital series featuring the Guardians of the Galaxy from the animated series in Infinite Comics format.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Chris Roberson and Rich Ellis's continuation of the Memorial series, following Emma in a world where the Lux Arcana and imaginary friends have become very real threats. Creative mythology-building in an accessible fantasy framework.
author: Chris Roberson

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel/Atlas' pre-code horror anthology (1953–1954) featuring short tales of horror and the macabre that epitomize the EC-influenced horror comics of the early 1950s. An important piece of Marvel's pre-superhero history, showcasing the horror tradition that briefly dominated American comics.
author: Stan Lee

subject: series
synopsis: A supernatural hero ensemble event exploring mystical warriors battling the vampire incursion.

subject: series
synopsis: Tove Jansson's beloved newspaper strip about the Moomin family — the original Swedish-Finnish comic strip collected by Drawn & Quarterly in beautiful archival editions. One of the great works of 20th-century cartooning, Jansson's warmth, philosophical depth, and extraordinary imagination created a world that has enchanted readers for 70 years.
author: Tove Jansson

subject: series
synopsis: Nick Spencer and Joe Eisma's mystery series following six gifted teenagers admitted to the elite Morning Glory Academy, which is secretly a sinister institution conducting mysterious experiments linked to time travel and ancient prophecy.
author: Nick Spencer

subject: series
synopsis: Jean Dufaux and Philippe Delaby's stunning historical comic set in ancient Rome following Lucius Murena, a young Roman caught in the political intrigue of Emperor Claudius' court and the machinations of the Imperial family.
author: Jean Dufaux

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's early golden-age anthology (1940–1942) featuring a rotating cast of masked heroes and supernatural figures in short adventure strips, representing Marvel's earliest publishing efforts. A historical artifact of American comics' original superhero boom.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Jean-David Morvan and Bengal's French thriller about Naja, an assassin who feels no pain, caught in a shadowy organization's war of killers.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series featuring Namor the Sub-Mariner in adventures formatted for the vertical reading experience on Marvel Unlimited.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Pat Mills and Kevin O'Neill's dystopian Gothic sci-fi follows Nemesis, a demonic alien warlock, leading a resistance against Torquemada — the fanatical alien-hating Grand Master of the space empire Termight — in the most visually transgressive British comics of the 1980s.
author: Pat Mills

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2025 Champions revival, bringing back the teen hero team in the post-Krakoa era with a mix of returning members and new faces. Part of Marvel's ongoing effort to maintain a viable young-heroes team title.
